sections.title: Employee Onboarding Process
sections.subtitle: Registration and legal setup in Eswatini

steps.title: Employment Contract Drafting
steps.description: Draft a localized contract compliant with the Employment Act of 1980. The contract must be provided in Swati or English and include clear terms on duties, hours, and compensation.

steps.title: Statutory Registration
steps.description: Register the employee with the Eswatini Revenue Service (ERS) for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) and the Graded Tax system.

steps.title: Social Security Enrollment
steps.description: Enroll employees in the Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF) if applicable, and ensure compliance with the Workers' Compensation Act.

steps.title: Work Permit Application
steps.description: For foreign nationals, apply for a work permit through the Ministry of Home Affairs. This process typically requires proof of skills that are not locally available.

steps.title: Bank Account Coordination
steps.description: While not strictly mandatory for foreign employers, local bank accounts for employees facilitate smoother payroll processing in Lilangeni (SZL).

items.title: Permanent Establishment Risk
items.text: Operating long-term without a legal entity may create tax liabilities. EOR is a common solution to mitigate this risk for up to 24 months.

items.title: Labor Law Compliance
items.text: The Employment Act of 1980 dictates strict notice periods and severance pay. Non-compliance can lead to hefty fines from the Industrial Court.

items.title: Local CBA Awareness
items.text: Certain industries in Eswatini have Collective Bargaining Agreements that may supersede general labor laws regarding minimum wage and leave.

items.title: Termination Grounds
items.text: Termination for misconduct requires a formal disciplinary hearing to withstand scrutiny in the Industrial Court.

items.title: Annual Leave Entitlement
items.text: Employees are entitled to 12 days of paid annual leave after completing one year of continuous service.

items.title: Sick Leave Provisions
items.text: Minimum 14 days at full pay and 14 days at half pay after three months of employment.

items.title: Maternity Protections
items.text: Expectant mothers are entitled to 12 weeks of maternity leave, usually with at least 1 year of service with the same employer.

items.title: Public Holiday Pay
items.text: Eswatini has 11+ public holidays; work performed on these days typically requires premium pay rates (2x).

faqs.question: Can I hire foreign workers through an EOR in Eswatini?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the EOR will need to sponsor the work permit. You must prove that the role cannot be filled by a local citizen.

faqs.question: What is the typical probation period?
faqs.answer: Probation is usually 3-6 months. During this period, termination is generally easier, but proper documentation is still advised.

faqs.question: Are bonuses mandatory in Eswatini?
faqs.answer: A 13th-month bonus is common in the private sector but not legally mandatory unless specified in the employment contract or CBA.

faqs.question: What is the notice period for senior roles?
faqs.answer: Notice periods vary by contract but typically range from 1 to 3 months for professional or managerial positions.

faqs.question: Is health insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: Private health insurance is not mandatory but highly recommended as a competitive benefit in the local market.

items.title: Governing Body
items.text: The Ministry of Labour and Social Security oversees all employment and labor relations in Eswatini.

items.title: Main Legislation
items.text: Employment Act No. 5 of 1980 and the Industrial Relations Act of 2000 form the core of labor law.

items.title: Social Security
items.text: Eswatini National Provident Fund (ENPF) and Workers' Compensation Act are the primary social security regulations.

steps.title: Data Collection
steps.description: Gather monthly inputs including overtime, bonuses, deductions, and unpaid leave records by the 20th of each month.

steps.title: Gross-to-Net Calculation
steps.description: Calculate gross salary, then apply PAYE tax bands, Graded Tax, and pension contributions to determine the net pay.

steps.title: Fund Distribution
steps.description: Execute payments to employees in Lilangeni (SZL). Ensure funds hit accounts by the last business day of the month.

steps.title: Tax Filing and Remittance
steps.description: Submit monthly PAYE returns (P38 form) and remit the withheld taxes to the Eswatini Revenue Service by the 7th of the following month.

steps.title: Annual Reconciliation
steps.description: File the annual PAYE reconciliation (P22 form) detailing all salaries and taxes paid throughout the fiscal year.

items.title: Late Payment Penalties
items.text: Failure to remit PAYE by the 7th of the month results in a 10% penalty plus interest on the outstanding amount.

items.title: Payslip Requirements
items.text: Every employee must receive a detailed payslip showing gross pay, all deductions, and the final net amount.

items.title: Lilangeni Currency Peg
items.text: The Lilangeni (SZL) is pegged 1:1 with the South African Rand (ZAR), which simplifies regional payroll but requires monitoring for exchange fluctuations.

items.title: Graded Tax Compliance
items.text: Graded tax is a mandatory monthly poll tax that must be deducted for every employed person over 18.

faqs.question: What is the fiscal year in Eswatini?
faqs.answer: The fiscal year for tax purposes runs from July 1st to June 30th.

faqs.question: Can I pay employees in USD?
faqs.answer: Legally, employees in Eswatini must be paid in Lilangeni (SZL). Central Bank approval is required for external payments.

faqs.question: Is severance pay mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, for employees with more than 12 months of service, severance is typically 10 days' pay for each year of service.

faqs.question: Are there special tax treatment for expats?
faqs.answer: Expats are generally taxed on Eswatini-sourced income. Double taxation agreements should be consulted.

steps.title: Gross Pay Calculation
steps.description: Sum of base salary, allowances (housing, transport), and any overtime or performance bonuses.

steps.title: Social Security (ENPF)
steps.description: Deduct 5% of gross salary, capped at SZL 200 per month for the employee (matched by the employer).

steps.title: PAYE Tax Calculation
steps.description: Apply the annualized progressive tax bands (0% to 33%) after deducting allowable pension contributions.

steps.title: Graded Tax Deduction
steps.description: Subtract the statutory Graded Tax of SZL 1.50 per month from the employee's net pay.

steps.title: Net Salary Payment
steps.description: The final amount is paid via bank transfer, and a compliant payslip is issued via software or email.

items.title: Social Security Cap 2025
items.text: As of Jan 1, 2025, the ENPF ceiling has increased, resulting in a max contribution of SZL 200 for both employer and employee.

items.title: Benefits-in-Kind
items.text: Company cars and housing provided to employees are taxable benefits and must be valued according to ERS schedules.

items.title: Termination Pay
items.text: Accrued leave and severance pay must be calculated accurately at the time of exit to avoid labor disputes.

items.title: Lilangeni-Rand Parity
items.text: The Lilangeni (SZL) is pegged 1:1 with the South African Rand (ZAR), simplifying regional payroll comparisons.

items.title: ENPF
items.text: National Provident Fund - 5% of pay up to E200.

items.title: PAYE
items.text: Pay-As-You-Earn income tax based on progressive bands.

items.title: Graded Tax
items.text: Statutory deduction of SZL 1.50 per month.

faqs.question: Is the 13th-month bonus included in the calculator?
faqs.answer: The calculator usually treats bonuses as additional taxable income in the month they are paid.

faqs.question: How do I handle medical aid deductions?
faqs.answer: Private medical aid is a voluntary deduction and is typically not tax-deductible in Eswatini for the employee.

faqs.question: What is the maximum tax rate for individuals?
faqs.answer: The top marginal tax rate is 33% for income exceeding SZL 200,000 per annum.

faqs.question: Does the calculator support part-time workers?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided their hours and hourly rates are converted into monthly gross equivalents.

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Apply for name reservation at the Registrar of Companies. The name must be unique and typically ends in '(Pty) Ltd' for private companies.

steps.title: Document Preparation
steps.description: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association. These documents must be signed by the initial shareholders and directors.

steps.title: Certificate of Incorporation
steps.description: Submit the finalized documents to the Registrar of Companies to obtain the official Certificate of Incorporation.

steps.title: Tax and VAT Registration
steps.description: Register the new entity with the Eswatini Revenue Service (ERS) for Corporate Tax and VAT (Value Added Tax).

steps.title: Trading License Application
steps.description: Apply for a trading license through the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Trade. This is required for most business operations.

steps.title: Bank Account Opening
steps.description: Open a local business bank account to facilitate share capital deposit and operational transactions.

items.title: Expatriate Director Vetting
items.text: Foreign directors and shareholders are subject to vetting by the Eswatini Investment Promotion Authority (EIPA) and security agencies.

items.title: Local Residency Requirement
items.text: While not strictly mandatory for all shareholders, having a local resident director significantly simplifies banking and tax registrations.

items.title: Incentive Programs
items.text: Companies in designated Special Economic Zones (SEZs) may benefit from tax holidays and customs duty exemptions.

items.title: Compliance Deadlines
items.text: Annual returns must be filed within 3 months of the company's financial year-end to avoid penalties.

items.title: (Pty) Ltd - Proprietary Limited
items.text: Most common for foreign investors. Limits liability and restricts share transfer.

items.title: Branch Office
items.text: An extension of a foreign company. Easier to set up but the parent company remains liable for all local debts.

items.title: Sole Proprietorship
items.text: Suitable for small businesses; owner has unlimited liability for all business obligations.

faqs.question: How long does it take to register a company in Eswatini?
faqs.answer: The full process, including tax registration and licensing, typically takes 4 to 6 weeks.

faqs.question: Is a local physical office required?
faqs.answer: Yes, every registered company must have a physical registered office address within Eswatini.

faqs.question: What is the minimum number of shareholders?
faqs.answer: A private limited company requires at least one shareholder and one director.

faqs.question: Can a foreign company own 100% of the local entity?
faqs.answer: Yes, 100% foreign ownership is allowed in most sectors, though some strategic sectors may have restrictions.

items.title: Importance of 'Swatification'

faqs.question: What is the typical time-to-hire in Eswatini?
faqs.answer: For professional roles, it usually ranges from 4 to 8 weeks depending on the seniority of the position.

faqs.question: Are there mandatory quotas for hiring locals?
faqs.answer: While not a hard quota, companies must demonstrate they've attempted to hire locals before being granted work permits for foreigners.

faqs.question: Is remote work common in Eswatini?
faqs.answer: It is becoming more common in the tech and NGO sectors, but many traditional businesses still prefer office-based roles.

faqs.question: What are the standard working hours?
faqs.answer: Typically 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday to Friday, totaling around 40-45 hours per week.

faqs.answer: Yes, provided the data is managed in accordance with the Data Protection Act 2022.

faqs.question: Can I integrate my HRIS with my bank?
faqs.answer: Many modern HRIS tools can generate bank-direct files (e.g., ABA or CSV) compatible with local banks like Nedbank or Standard Bank.

faqs.question: Does the system handle the 13th-month bonus?
faqs.answer: Most systems can be configured to automate the 13th-month calculation, which is common but not mandatory in Eswatini.

faqs.question: What about tracking work permits?

steps.title: Year-End Closing

steps.title: External Audit

steps.title: Financial Statement Filing

items.title: IFRS Adoption
items.text: Eswatini has fully adopted IFRS Standards for both domestic and foreign companies, ensuring global comparability.

items.title: VAT Threshold
items.text: Registration for VAT is mandatory if annual taxable turnover exceeds SZL 500,000. Voluntary registration is possible for smaller entities.

items.title: Fiscal Year Alignment
items.text: The standard fiscal year ends on June 30th. Companies can apply to the ERS for a different year-end if needed for global consolidation.

items.title: Record Retention

items.title: Registrar of Companies

items.title: SIA (Swaziland Institute of Accountants)

items.title: IFRS for SMEs
items.text: Permitted for smaller companies that do not have public accountability.

faqs.question: Is an audit mandatory for all companies?
faqs.answer: Yes, most private companies ((Pty) Ltd) in Eswatini are required to have their annual financial statements audited by a registered auditor.

faqs.question: What is the VAT rate in Eswatini?
faqs.answer: The standard VAT rate is 15%, which applies to most goods and services.

faqs.question: Can I keep my books in USD?
faqs.answer: For local tax and statutory reporting, financial statements must be presented in Lilangeni (SZL).

faqs.question: How do I ensure tax compliance for a foreign branch?
faqs.answer: Foreign branches are taxed on Eswatini-sourced income at the same rates as domestic companies, but may be subject to branch profits tax.

steps.title: Business License Renewal

steps.title: Data Protection Registration

steps.title: Labor Inspection Readiness

steps.title: ENPF Compliance

steps.title: Environmental Impact Assessments

items.title: Data Protection Act 2022

items.title: Industrial Relations Act
items.text: The Act grants strong rights to trade unions. Maintaining positive labor relations is key to avoiding prolonged industrial action.

items.title: ESG Reporting
items.text: While not yet mandatory for all, larger corporations are increasingly adopting ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) reporting standards.

items.title: FICA Compliance
items.text: Financial institutions and certain businesses must adhere to strict Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) rules.

items.title: EDPA

items.title: ENPF

items.title: FSC

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the 72-hour breach reporting window?
faqs.answer: The EDPA can levy significant administrative fines, and directors may held personally liable for negligence.

faqs.question: Is it mandatory to have health and safety committee?
faqs.answer: Yes, for companies with more than 20 employees, a workplace safety committee is a legal requirement.

faqs.question: How often are business licenses inspected?
faqs.answer: Inspections are typically unannounced and happen at least once a year or upon renewal.

faqs.question: Can I store employee data outside Eswatini?
faqs.answer: Cross-border data transfer is allowed if the receiving country has adequate data protection laws, subject to EDPA approval.

steps.title: Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Filing
steps.description: Returns must be submitted within 120 days from June 30th (the end of the fiscal year). For 2025, the standard rate is 25%.

steps.title: PAYE Monthly Remittance
steps.description: Employers must remit Pay-As-You-Earn tax withheld from employees to ERS by the 7th of the following month.

steps.title: VAT Returns
steps.description: Value Added Tax (15%) returns and payments are due by the 20th of the month following the tax period via the TaxEase portal.

steps.title: Provisional Tax Payments
steps.description: Paid in two installments: the first by December 31st and the second by June 30th.

steps.title: Annual Withholding Tax Reconciliation
steps.description: Submit annual reconciliations for withholding taxes on dividends, interest, and management fees paid to non-residents.

items.title: TaxEase Platform
items.text: The Eswatini Revenue Service (ERS) has fully transitioned to TaxEase for all filings. Ensuring valid digital credentials is now mandatory.

items.title: Transfer Pricing Rules
items.text: Eswatini has implemented stricter transfer pricing regulations. Documentation is required for all cross-border intra-group transactions.

items.title: SEZ Tax Holidays
items.text: Companies registered in Special Economic Zones may qualify for a 0% corporate tax rate for the first 20 years.

items.title: Non-Resident Management Fees
items.text: A 15% withholding tax applies to management or consultant fees paid to non-residents, often a point of audit by the ERS.

items.title: Tax Identification Number (TIN)
items.text: Required for all business transactions, bank account openings, and import/export licenses.

items.title: VAT Invoice Compliance
items.text: Invoices must include specific details: TIN, registered address, and a clear breakdown of the 15% VAT.

items.title: Audited Financials
items.text: Must be attached to the annual income tax return for all registered companies.

faqs.question: Are there capital gains taxes in Eswatini?
faqs.answer: Eswatini does not have a separate Capital Gains Tax, but some gains may be included in taxable income depending on the frequency of transactions.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late VAT filing?
faqs.answer: Late filing attracts a penalty of 10% of the tax due, plus interest at the prevailing market rate.

faqs.question: Does Eswatini have Double Tax Agreements (DTAs)?
faqs.answer: Yes, Eswatini has DTAs with several countries including South Africa, the UK, and Taiwan to prevent double taxation.

faqs.question: Can I claim input VAT on company vehicles?
faqs.answer: Generally, input VAT on passenger vehicles is not deductible unless the company is in the business of selling or hiring vehicles.

faqs.question: Which social platform is most popular in Eswatini?
faqs.answer: Facebook is the most widely used social media platform for both business and personal connections.

faqs.question: Is influencer marketing viable in Eswatini?
faqs.answer: Yes, there is a growing group of local lifestyle and business influencers who can drive significant engagement.

faqs.question: Do I need a local agency to run ads?
faqs.answer: While you can run digital ads remotely, a local agency is invaluable for traditional media buy and cultural alignment.

faqs.question: What are the restrictions on advertising?
faqs.answer: Alcohol and tobacco advertising have specific legal restrictions, and all ads must comply with the Swaziland Standards Authority guidelines.
